column3: 1. Is the prohibition of non-intervention a norm of customary international law?
column4: 2. Is the scope of the principle of non-intervention uncertain?
column5: 3. Does the prohibition of non-intervention apply to cyber-operations?
column6: 4. Is coercion a constituent element of prohibited intervention?
column7: 4.1   Is coercion limited to the employment of physical force?
column8: 4.2   Can dictatorial demands or acts of compulsion or imposition constitute coercion?
column9: 4.3   Does the deprivation of a State’s ability to control matters within its domaine réservé amount to coercion?
column10: 4.4   Does coercion extend to any affirmative acts designed to deprive another state of its freedom of choice with regard to a matter of protected sovereign prerogative?
column11: 4.5 Must there be a causal nexus between the responsible state’s actions/efforts and the effects on the target state’s internal or external affairs?
column12: 4.6 Can attempts to coerce an outcome amount to prohibited intervention?
column13: 4.7   Is intent a constituent element of coercion?
column14: 4.8 Must the action(s) constituting coercion be designed/intended to influence outcomes in, or conduct with respect to, a matter of protected sovereign prerogative?
column16: 4.10   Must the target state have knowledge of the coercive cyber operation constituting the purported intervention?
column17: 5. Does intervention include forms of persuasion or propaganda?
column18: 6. Is there a de minimis exception to the prohibition?
column19: 7. Must the intervention be directed at matters over which the victim state is permitted by the principle of sovereignty, to decide freely?
column20: 7.1   Does the zone of protected sovereign prerogatives include only internal affairs?
column21: 7.2   Does the prohibition proscribe intervention in a state’s external (foreign) affairs?
column22: 7.3   Is the zone of protected sovereign prerogatives referred to as domaine réservé?
column23: 7.4   Is the domaine réservé limited to matters involving the state’s choice of a political, economic, social, and cultural system, and the formulation of foreign policy?
column24: 7.5   Does international law regulation over a matter of sovereign prerogative remove it from the domaine réservé?
column25: 7.6   Is critical infrastructure part of the domaine réservé?
column26: 7.7   Are elections part of the domaine réservé?
column27: 7.8   Is the operation of legislatures a part of the domaine réservé?
column28: 7.9  Is financial system stability part of the domaine réservé?
column29: 7.10  Are medical services part of the domaine réservé?
